applied.old: No — because phosphate has valency 3 and ammonium has valency 1, so we always need exactly 3 ammonium ions to balance one phosphate ion — the ratio is fixed by valency.
applied.new: No — DAP contains the hydrogen phosphate ion, HPO₄²⁻, which has valency 2, and ammonium has valency 1, so we always need exactly 2 ammonium ions: (NH₄)₂HPO₄. In ammonium phosphate, PO₄³⁻ has valency 3, so it needs exactly 3: (NH₄)₃PO₄. The ratio is fixed by valency.
